title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 7
statement: Six points are equally spaced around a circle of radius \(1.\) Three of these points are the vertices of a triangle that is neither equilateral nor isosceles. What is the area of this triangle?

solutions.text:
Six equally spaced points on the circle form a regular hexagon. A triangle using three of them is not equilateral or isosceles only when its angles are \(30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ\).

The hypotenuse is a diameter of the unit circle, so it has length \(2\). The legs of the \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle are \(1\) and \(\sqrt3\).

The area is \(\frac12\cdot1\cdot\sqrt3=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\).

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: The only allowed non-isosceles triangle from six equally spaced points is a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle
Use the diameter as the hypotenuse
